title: Push senderDisplayName fallback chain ignores SpaceMember.nick in channel chats
description:
File: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-push-00.md, line 170-171

The push draft defines:

  `senderDisplayName` (String, optional):
  : The sender's display name at push-generation time. Derived from `ChatContact.displayName` if present, otherwise `ChatContact.login`, otherwise `senderId`.

For channel chats, the main draft establishes a richer display-name precedence:

- SpaceMember has a `nick` field (draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00.md line 599):
    `nick` (String, optional):
    : Space-specific display name override. MAY be absent; clients SHOULD fall back to ChatContact `displayName`, then `login`.

The intended UX semantics: in a Space, a user's display name is their per-Space nick if set; otherwise the global ChatContact.displayName; otherwise login. The push draft's fallback chain omits the nick rung entirely, so a push notification for a channel chat will not match what the user sees inside the Space's chat UI when the sender has a Space-specific nick. Example: in an ACME Space, a user known globally as "Robert Smith" might have `nick: "Bob (CEO)"` in that Space; the in-app message header would read "Bob (CEO)" but the push notification would read "Robert Smith".

This is editorial drift, not a wire-protocol break: clients can override display anyway. But for fidelity with the SpaceMember.nick model and consistency with what end users see, the push draft fallback chain for channel chats SHOULD be: SpaceMember.nick (when sender is a SpaceMember of the containing Space) -> ChatContact.displayName -> ChatContact.login -> senderId.

For direct and group chats, SpaceMember is not in play; the existing fallback is correct as-is.

Suggested wording (line 171):

  `senderDisplayName` (String, optional):
  : The sender's display name at push-generation time. For `chatKind: "channel"`, derived from the sender's `SpaceMember.nick` in the containing Space if present, otherwise `ChatContact.displayName` if present, otherwise `ChatContact.login`, otherwise `senderId`. For other chat kinds, derived from `ChatContact.displayName` if present, otherwise `ChatContact.login`, otherwise `senderId`. The `senderId` fallback occurs when the ChatContact record has not yet been fully resolved -- for example, when a message arrives from a previously unknown peer in a federated deployment. This value is a snapshot and may become stale; clients MUST NOT treat it as an authoritative identity signal.
acceptance_criteria:
- Push draft senderDisplayName definition includes SpaceMember.nick as the first rung of the fallback chain for channel chats
- Direct and group chats keep the existing fallback (SpaceMember does not apply there)
- Wording is consistent with main draft line 599-600 client-side fallback guidance
- No new fields introduced; this is purely a clarification of the derivation rule on the server side
